reason: The base JIT fastpass still assigns the value written by a swallowed issue for an absent optional property, so the successful result incorrectly contains the key.
The pull request guards the JIT assignment when an optional property is absent, while preserving failure for a present invalid value, matching the expected behavior.
Before the change, the paragraph rule recognizes spaces-only blank lines but not a tab-only line, so the two text lines are merged.
The revised paragraph lookahead treats one or more spaces or tabs as a blank line, producing separate paragraphs.
The tested JSON response parsing is unrelated to the pull request's error-stack decoration change and remains normal behavior.
The pull request only hardens request error stack decoration and does not affect successful JSON response parsing.
Parsing a normal boolean flag does not depend on the negative-number exponent detector changed by this pull request.
The uppercase-exponent fix is unrelated to recognizing an ordinary boolean option flag, which continues to parse successfully.
The base revision still accepts the non-ASCII digit string during tree-to-integer conversion, contrary to the expected rejection.
The revised integer readers reject non-ASCII digits in string values, matching the test expectation.
Before the fix, the Postgres search-path parser splits the configured string rather than preserving a hyphenated or accented schema as one name.
The pull request fixes search-path parsing so the configured hyphenated or accented schema is applied as a single name.
Image transformation eligibility is unrelated to the ByteBuffer exception cleanup change.
The resource-leak fix does not change whether configured image transformations are eligible.
Caching the allowed-symbol character set does not change the naming rule's acceptance of a configured symbol.
The head revision only caches derived name-configuration data, preserving the configured-symbol behavior.
SVG data-URI image loading is unrelated to adding the missing C++ standard header for GCC compilation.
The Afrikaans locale translation change does not affect daylight-saving arithmetic.
The GCC header fix has no effect on browser SVG data-URI loading.
The form decoder's empty optional body behavior is unrelated to parsing multiple Cookie headers.
The Cookie-header parsing change does not alter decoding an empty form body into an optional-only type.
A spelling-only change does not affect removal of non-empty directories from an in-memory filesystem.
The spelling corrections are unrelated to filesystem removal semantics.
Passing JSON flags as depth is unrelated to schema comparison of equivalent indexes.
The head change remains unrelated to the comparator's handling of equally valid index renames.
Adding Afrikaans week translations does not affect daylight-saving datetime shifting.
The circuit-breaker predicate exception fix is unrelated to rate-limiter replenishment after lowering its limit.
The revised circuit-breaker cleanup does not change the independent rate-limiter behavior described by the test.
The prefer-template ASI autofix change is unrelated to var hoisting behavior in the described function.
The pull request only inserts semicolons for template-literal autofixes and does not alter declaration accessibility.
The logging argument-formatting change does not affect persisted sitemap-job restart behavior.
The head revision changes only log formatter argument handling, not spider restart lifecycle behavior.
Bidi-control sanitization is unrelated to narrow-terminal highlighted-line rendering.
The sanitize change does not affect whether a themed narrow terminal line aborts rendering.
Optimizing an RFC5424 regular expression does not change metadata-based output symlink creation.
The structured-data parsing optimization is unrelated to later symlink updates for a metadata key.
Changing platform-thread waiting behavior for virtual-thread efficiency is unrelated to connection-pool creation and system-property locking.
The ConcurrentBag virtual-thread optimization does not change the described concurrent pool startup behavior.
The SORT ACL key-check fix is unrelated to Redis background-save behavior on a growing 32-bit dataset.
The ACL parser change does not affect systemd persistence or background saves.
The current-directory bookkeeping fix is unrelated to preserving large-number digit editing with CTRL-A.
The head change concerns window CWD restoration and does not affect CTRL-X numeric editing.
The file-cache reclamation race fix is unrelated to array concatenation with NULL.
The cache-block lifetime change does not alter list concatenation result types.
Touchscreen ScrollBar input handling is unrelated to RefCounted pre-delete notification validity.
The ScrollBar input fix does not affect releasing the last RefCounted reference.
Rejecting categorical absolute-error features is unrelated to regression metrics on constant columns.
The categorical-feature validation change does not affect near-constant-column r_regression warnings.
The Swagger readonly-field fix is unrelated to Vault Agent token sink file modes.
Removing stale Swagger readonly attributes does not change token-file permissions.
The base HelpFormatter still produces the spurious usage-line formatting that this test rejects.
The revised HelpFormatter normalizes separators and removes the spurious usage characters, matching the expected usage line.
Returning a plain dictionary as JSON is unrelated to IPv6 host/port parsing in the development server and test client.
The IPv6 parsing fix does not change dictionary-to-JSON response conversion.
Missing required-field reporting is unrelated to generic-alias hashability during schema generation.
The generic-alias fix does not alter the expected missing-field validation error.
Replacing logging.WARN with logging.WARNING preserves the logging level and does not change routine SQL echo suppression.
The logging constant rename is behavior-preserving for default SQL echo output.
Making lazy attribute method definition thread-safe does not change computed-attribute access cost or semantics.
The thread-safety refactor leaves the computed versus column attribute behavior unchanged.
Before the change, each dispatch leaves a distinct called wrapper in the call stack, so two invocations yield two entries.
The new implementation deliberately deduplicates called listeners, so two invocations of one listener produce one entry rather than the expected two.
The shellcheck cleanup does not change how custom completion hooks identify sibling subcommands.
The revised completion script only preserves shell words and handles failed pushd, not the current-command selection logic.
The existing query parser already combines repeated keys into an array, and the dependency update does not invalidate that expectation.
The qs dependency update preserves repeated-key arrays in the default parser mode.
In the base revision get_environ_proxies accepts a single URL argument and returns the proxy mapping as expected.
The head revision changes get_environ_proxies to require a no_proxy argument, so the documented one-argument call raises a missing-argument error.
The parser change targets numeric unit values such as .5sec, not a bare .foons word in a list.
Adding support for leading-dot numeric unit values does not make a bare .foons list item fail to parse as a string.
Before the change the cURL handler connects a sink for HEAD requests, which is the faulty path targeted by this regression fix.
The head revision skips sink setup for HEAD requests, avoiding the cURL failure and allowing the request to complete.
The base diff formatter mishandles maps embedded in list assertions, causing the improper-list match failure to crash or lose its standard diff.
The revised formatter converts inserted and deleted maps to the appropriate AST representation, preserving a clear match-failure diff.
The base implementation has the dynamic CSS-prop hydration bug, so the nested component loses its scoped custom property after re-rendering.
The head revision applies the dynamic CSS property hydration fix and preserves the scoped property after re-rendering.
Using hook filters in internal plugins is unrelated to static-asset handling for a multiline new URL expression.
The plugin hook refactor does not alter the bundler's multiline new URL asset detection.
The base version does not export the current NUL-delimited item to child preview processes, so the preview command cannot run with the required item.
The head revision exports FZF_CURRENT_ITEM, allowing preview commands to receive items containing NUL data under the NUL delimiter.
The pre-change deprecated-view-flag implementation leaves system bars unrestored when switching from immersiveSticky to edgeToEdge.
The revised implementation uses the edge-to-edge APIs and restores the system bars on the mode switch.
The base pattern parser still reports the multiple-assignment syntax error for the class-keyword binding case.
The head revision contains the syntax-error fix, so the valid case pattern is accepted without an error.
The base decoder assumes the pre-populated slice is already large enough and panics when decoding the two nested blocks.
The revised decoder grows the destination slice as needed, so repeated nested blocks decode successfully.
Before the fix, mocked now retains the mock moment's timezone when no timezone is requested instead of using the application default.
The head revision falls back to the application's default timezone for an unqualified mocked current time.
The base protocol-relative URL regular expression misses the unusual leading-slash forms described by the test.
The expanded regular expression recognizes the additional protocol-relative slash and whitespace forms.
Changing hash-combination internals from a copying accessor to an internal accessor does not change MD5 digest values.
The performance refactor is value-preserving and unrelated to computing the well-known MD5 digest.
Moving diagnostic descriptors to a dedicated class preserves supported HTTP-method client generation.
The diagnostic refactor does not change successful generation for an interface with a supported HTTP verb.
Removing redundant final continue statements does not change HTTP/1.1 response-body fetching.
The loop cleanup preserves control flow, so fetching a plain response body remains successful.
The base conversion loses the requested basic format when converting a non-ISO calendar date.
The fix preserves the requested basic ISO format for dates using a custom calendar.
Before the fix, changing the period end date leaves the native end property at its original value.
The revised period update synchronizes the native end property with the changed end date.
The base URL normalizer permits embedded whitespace in the request path, so a newline can reach the request line instead of being rejected.
The head revision rejects whitespace in the resolved path or host before sending the request.
The Albanian million pluralization change is unrelated to converting whole numbers to English words.
The locale-specific Albanian change does not affect English number-to-words output.
Ignoring non-string system properties is unrelated to resolving a singleton dependency from a DI module.
The property-loading fix does not change normal singleton dependency resolution.
The shared replace primitive is described as behavior-preserving and does not change ordered-dictionary element replacement.
The refactored implementation preserves the ordered dictionary replace operation's behavior.
Replacing the manual nonnegative clamp with built-in max preserves invalid size parsing behavior.
The max/min simplification is semantically equivalent for the invalid size value described.
The base case-insensitive path search can select the static child instead of the trailing wildcard child and panic for this route layout.
The head revision selects the wildcard child from the end of the child list, preventing the invalid-node panic and resolving the redirect.
The base Numeric.Int64Value path dereferences a nil Int for a valid empty numeric and panics instead of returning zero.
The nil guard in toBigInt makes a valid numeric with no integer value convert to zero.
Restoring hard-tab renderer tab stops is unrelated to prompt shutdown from outside the update loop.
The renderer tab-stop initialization change does not alter the program's external-quit handling.
Before the cancellation-order fix, an already-cancelled token can still poll the wrapped future rather than skip it entirely.
The revised cancellation wrapper checks the token first and skips polling an already-cancelled operation.
Skipping unreachable ignore files does not change case-insensitive matching for a reachable file.
The ignore-file traversal optimization is unrelated to the case-insensitive pattern matcher.
Removing one nesting level is presented as a refactor and does not change the default value supplied to a skipped field.
The head refactor preserves deserialization semantics for an omitted skipped field.
